name: Antoine Ouilmette's household at his house west of the Kinzies
head: ouilmette_antoine
review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi woman (Currey) married to a French trader, whose household stayed through the battle. The card states only what the named sources say.

present_on_scene_date.note: The household stayed through the battle (Wau-Bun; Quaife).

associated_with.note: The house the 1812 structure record calls Ouilmette's; the sources differ on whether it stood north, behind or west of the Kinzie house (civilians.json notes).

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3461 sweep found in this household on 14 August is on the card.

persons.name: Antoine Ouilmette

present_on_scene_date.note: No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Portage carrier; employee of Kinzie. Ancestry as the sources put it: French (Canadian), per Wau-Bun and Quaife. Stayed in his own house through the evacuation; the only white resident left after 18 Aug. Not enrolled in the militia. After 14 August: Remained at Chicago through the war; found there by the 1816 garrison; Gros Point (Wilmette) reservation 1829; died at Council Bluffs.

evidence.quote: Ouilmette claimed to have come to Chicago in 1790.
he was living with his Indian wife in one of the four huts which they found here

persons.name: Archange Ouilmette

present_on_scene_date.note: No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Ancestry as the sources put it: Potawatomi per Currey; "half-breed" per Wau-Bun. Watched the troops leave from the north side (Head Papers account); the household stayed. After 14 August: Granted land with her children at Prairie du Chien 1829; died at Council Bluffs.

persons.name: The Ouilmette children

present_on_scene_date.note: No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: One row for the children of the house, who are counted and not named for 1812. Currey counts "half-breed children of Ouilmette" in the winter of 1812-13. Andreas names Elizabeth, Josette, Michell, Lewis, Francis, Sophie and Joseph, but gives no birth years; Josette was a child in 1831, so she was not yet born. After 14 August: Later to Kansas with the Potawatomi (Andreas).

evidence.quote: including the half-breed children of Ouilmette and the engagés and helpers in the employ of Du Pin
Michell, Lewis, Francis, Sophie and Joseph
